public_body: Fall River Housing Authority Board Of Commissioners
overall: Violations found: insufficient notice (unnamed union), voice vote to enter executive session, improper executive session topics (two of four), late minutes approval, late response to complaints. Ordered release of part of Feb. 13 minutes.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 notice listed 'Union Negotiations' without naming the bargaining unit, allegedly too vague for the public.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the notice of the February 13, 2023, meeting contained insufficient specificity by failing to include this information and therefore the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 notice gave a range of executive session minutes to approve (Sept. 2021 to Dec. 2022) rather than specific minutes.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

allegations.summary: Dec. 12, 2022 executive session convening: complainant alleged the chair did not announce the purpose and no roll call was taken, and the recording stopped before the vote.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board complied with the Open Meeting Law’s procedural requirements for convening in executive session on December 12, 2022.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 vote to enter executive session was taken by voice ('all in favor') rather than by roll call.
allegations.key_passage: This was a violation of the Open Meeting Law as the law specifically requires that the vote of each member to enter executive session be by roll call.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 executive session allegedly improper: discussed Executive Director evaluation and Executive Team Restructuring under Purpose 2.
allegations.key_passage: Performance evaluations and discussions of an employee’s professional competence must occur in open session as they do not fit within any of the ten permissible purposes to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 executive session 'Union Negotiations' discussion under Purpose 3 challenged as improper.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the discussions in executive session that related to “Union Negotiations” under Purpose 3 were appropriate as the Board discussed its strategy with respect to a collective bargaining agreement with the municipal employees’ union.

allegations.summary: Feb. 13, 2023 executive session 'HUD Audit Update' discussion under Purpose 7 challenged as improper.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the discussions pertaining to the “HUD Audit Update” were appropriate under Purpose 7.

allegations.summary: Dec. 12, 2022 executive session under Purpose 5 for 'a Personnel Matter' was not raised by complainants; AG raised the concern on its own.
allegations.key_passage: “personnel” is not an appropriate reason to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to timely approve executive session minutes from Sept. 2021 through Dec. 2022 until Feb. 13, 2023.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve these minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to review and respond within 14 business days to two earlier Open Meeting Law complaints filed in Feb. and March 2023.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board did not respond to the complaints until April 5, 2023, we find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Within 30 days, publicly release the portion of the February 13, 2023 executive session minutes pertaining to 'Executive Director Evaluation' and 'Executive Team Restructuring', without redaction or withholding.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements; similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: we order the Board, within 30 days of this letter, to publicly release the portion of the February 13, 2023, executive session minutes that pertained to the topics “Executive Director Evaluation” and “Executive Team Restructuring.”

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
